day-87-act-01.title: Fixed Evaluation Protocol and Honest Metrics
day-87-act-01.prerequisites: Day 86 integrated harness and baseline ledger.
day-87-act-01.objective: Freeze the evaluation before any tuning run: task order, metric definitions, and the evidence kinds (deterministic-fixture vs live-model-run) that keep simulated and real results from being merged.
day-87-act-01.instructions:
1. Re-open capstone_acceptance.json: the task set, metrics, and ceilings are now frozen - post-hoc edits void the evaluation.
2. Define per-task reporting exactly like live_eval_contract.json: status, steps, retries, termination, report hash; label every live field evidence_kind=live-model-run and every fixture field evidence_kind=deterministic-fixture.
3. Predeclare the comparison rule: deterministic runs must match the baseline ledger; authorized live runs are compared per task against it, and differences are recorded, not hidden.
4. Plan coverage honestly: at least one success task plus every malformed-request and failure task - never only attractive examples.
5. Handle missing evidence explicitly: a task not run is status=not-run, never silently dropped.
6. Write eval_protocol.md: the frozen rules a reviewer can audit against the results table.
day-87-act-01.exercise_prompt: Write eval_protocol.md with the frozen task list, the metric table, the evidence_kind labeling rule, and the not-run policy; then predict the results-table shape before running anything.
day-87-act-01.hint: Borrow the label discipline from ticket 23: if a field cannot tell which world it came from, it will eventually lie for you.
day-87-act-01.answer: The protocol names every task, metric, and ceiling before execution; the results table has one row per task carrying evidence_kind; absent runs are marked not-run. Any post-hoc criterion change is a new protocol version, not an edit.
day-87-act-01.mastery_criterion: Deliver a protocol under which results, regressions, and missing evidence all have predefined, auditable slots.

day-87-act-02.title: Capstone Evidence Package Assembly
day-87-act-02.prerequisites: Day 87 Activity 1 frozen protocol; all Day 85-86 artifacts.
day-87-act-02.objective: Assemble the sanitized evidence package a reviewer can audit end-to-end: charter, contract, baseline ledger, per-task results, failure log, resource accounting, provenance table, and a privacy pass.
day-87-act-02.instructions:
1. Create capstone_evidence/ with index.md listing every artifact and what it proves.
2. Attach: charter_review.json, capstone_acceptance.json, baseline_ledger.md, the per-task results table, fault_drill.json, and delivery_log.md.
3. Add resource accounting: wall time per run, total steps/retries, token and cost fields left null until an authorized live run; note continuing storage charges per the pretraining evidence plan.
4. Build the provenance table: model id plus license, dataset origin plus hash, the cited source registry ids, and the repository licenses (Apache-2.0 code, CC BY-SA 4.0 content).
5. Run the privacy pass: scan file contents for tokens, keys, emails, and absolute home paths; redact before packaging - provider identifiers stay in private notes, never in the repository.
6. Validate: a reviewer starting at index.md reaches every claim's evidence in one hop.
day-87-act-02.exercise_prompt: Produce capstone_evidence/index.md plus the provenance table citing at least the five referenced artifacts (agent project, LoRA comparison contract, live-eval contract, pretraining evidence package, CI practice runner), and record the privacy-scan result.
day-87-act-02.hint: Every claim needs a pointer and every pointer must resolve; the privacy scan covers file contents, not just filenames.
day-87-act-02.answer: The index maps claim - artifact - result. Provenance cites projects/agent_learning, projects/lora/evidence/comparison_contract.json, projects/agent_learning/evidence/live_eval_contract.json, curriculum/projects/docs/pretrain-cloud-evidence/evidence-package.json, and scripts/ci_practice_runner.py with their licenses. The privacy scan reports zero secrets.
day-87-act-02.mastery_criterion: Assemble a package where every claim resolves to stored evidence and the provenance and privacy tables are complete.

day-87-act-03.title: Post-Mortem, Failure Taxonomy, and Controlled Recovery
day-87-act-03.objective: Write the blameless capstone post-mortem: a failure taxonomy, honest treatment of unmet criteria and regressions, live-versus-simulated scoping, and a demonstrated controlled recovery.
day-87-act-03.instructions:
1. Group every observed failure into the taxonomy: malformed_tool_request, missing_input, loop, budget_exhausted, provider_or_infra, evaluation_defect.
2. For each class record symptom, trace pointer, root cause, and the fix or the accepted limitation. Unmet acceptance criteria stay unmet - label them; do not narrate over them.
3. State live-versus-simulated scope explicitly: deterministic results prove harness behavior; live-model fields remain null and blocked until authorization - no simulation is presented as a real run.
4. Demonstrate one controlled recovery end-to-end: break a fixture, observe the health-check failure, restore the known-good artifact, re-verify by hash; attach the before and after hashes.
5. Note residual risk: billing or storage follow-ups, stale-content revalidation, and what a reviewer could not check.
6. Save postmortem.md and link it from the evidence index.
day-87-act-03.exercise_prompt: Produce postmortem.md with the six-class taxonomy table, one worked recovery with hashes, an explicit unmet-criteria list (or the literal word 'none'), and the residual-risk paragraph.
day-87-act-03.hint: Blameless means the taxonomy names conditions and controls, not people; the strongest line is the one admitting what is still unproven.
day-87-act-03.answer: The post-mortem groups all drill faults by class, marks live-model acceptance items blocked-awaiting-authorization, shows restore-hash equality for the recovery, and lists residual risks including billing lag and reviewer-unchecked areas.
day-87-act-03.mastery_criterion: Deliver a post-mortem where failures are classified with evidence, unmet criteria remain visible, and recovery is proven rather than claimed.

day-87-act-04.title: Assessment: Dual-Rubric Acceptance and Submission
day-87-act-04.objective: Judge the capstone under two separate rubrics - the Independent Mastery Check rubric for unaided work and the Agent-Assisted Engineering Check rubric for directed work - then submit the evidence package through the project submission form.
day-87-act-04.instructions:
1. Apply the independent rubric to the work done unaided (charter gate, baseline ledger, evidence assembly, this review): each item is scored on correctness plus evidence pointers.
2. Apply the assisted rubric to directed work (integration design, CI rehearsal, post-mortem): scored on direction quality, diff inspection, and correction handling - never on agent output alone.
3. Verify the separation rule: independent mastery must not be inferred from assisted output; record both rubric totals and their scopes separately.
4. Submit below: repository link, report link, and notes summarizing commands re-run and hashes observed - pasted logs are self-reported evidence and the form labels them as such.
5. Distinguish acceptance layers: this learner project acceptance grades your work; the platform Course Readiness Gate (all 90 days, four language editions, platform behavior, ticket 61) is a separate later acceptance - a passing capstone does not declare the course ready.
6. Record the final verdict in capstone_verdict.json.
day-87-act-04.exercise_prompt: Submit the capstone evidence (repository link, report link, notes) in the form below, then produce capstone_verdict.json with both rubric scores, their scopes, and the explicit statement separating project acceptance from Course Readiness.
day-87-act-04.hint: The rubric column you cannot fill honestly is the column you must leave unclaimed.
day-87-act-04.answer: Verdict example: independent 4/4 checks with evidence pointers; assisted 3/3 with direction artifacts; the submission is recorded as self-reported evidence pending deterministic verification; 'capstone accepted' does not equal 'course ready' - the gate lives in ticket 61.
day-87-act-04.mastery_criterion: Pass only when both rubrics are scored separately with evidence, the submission is recorded honestly, and the Course Readiness Gate distinction is stated in the verdict.
